@pleerock
i like this approach but it seems like this wouldn't work nicely with a `@column` property?

@Asarew the `@Column` decorator defines a column in the database. The `addSelectAndMap` is a feature that calculates a virtual field in **a specific query**. In other words, this property should not be part of the entity, just part of the query itself. If you are using Typescript it's good practice to define the property in an interface or in the class, but since this property is not part of the actual table, you should not use the `@Column` decorator.

If you define a virtual column with this decorator you can create inconsistencies between the entities and the database tables. The `@Column` decorator is used as a way to sync your model with your database table, in this case these properties won't be part of the table, so there's no reason to use it.

My only concern with your approach is when you use `addSelectAndMap` on a property that is actually in the table, that it bypasses all existing(& future) logic. I opened up a [PR](https://github.com/TwenixPlatform/typeorm/pull/1) to amend the test to highlight what i mean. So maybe a simple fix would be to incorporate my PR(#4703) into yours somehow?

I think you're confused about the functionality of this feature. This feature **calculate a virtual column. The virtual columns doesn't exists in any table. In no case do these fields have to do with anything in the database tables.**

If you want to select a specific property that is actually in the table you will use the `select()` or `addSelect()` methods from queryBuilder object. You can use this methods together with the `addSelectAndMap` function. You can see this in my examples.

I think isn't a good idea use your PR. The typeorm developers commented that it was not a good solution because it could create inconsistencies with the database tables and it would be necessary to modify the structure of the models when it should not have anything to do. In my opinion I think you are confusing your approach.

You were correct and i miss understood your feature. 

I would improve the type conversion of the value so that you don't have to update all database drivers. Let the user only pass in a function instead of string for argument `columnType`.

issue_context.title: select additional computed columns
issue_context.body:
assuming i have some table with a column name, that may be null
in a query i would want to have a computed column "hasName", that is true if the name field is not null

i could do that as follows with the query builder
```
... createQueryBuilder("person")
.addSelect("name IS NOT NULL as hasName")
```
this is of course not mapped, and therefore only visible in "getRawMany()" .. but it shows what i want to achieve.


assume now i have a query for orders

```
... createQueryBuilder("order")
.leftJoinAndSelect("order.person", "person")
.addSelect("person.name IS NOT NULL as person.hasName") // does NOT work
```

question1: can addSelect be mapped to a custom variable, like it can be done with leftJoinAndMapOne?
question2: is there something like addSelectAndMap?
